# task-management · per-folder lists

Only when the `task_lists:` block in `<merlin-manifest>` says `state: active`.
Without that line, use `SKILL.md` in this folder as written and ignore this
file.

The engine is the folder `<plugin-root>/lib/engine/triage-tasks`, written
`<engine>` below. Everything in `SKILL.md` about ids, tags, sections, the line
shape, the `ops.json` actions and the three rules the engine enforces still
holds. What changes is where tasks live and how the engine is told where they
go.

## How it is laid out

- **Each project folder keeps its own list:** a `TASKS.md` at the root of that
  folder, with its own id prefix. A task in the Website folder gets an id like
  `WS12`. The `folders:` rows in the `task_lists:` block name each folder, its
  prefix and its path. Below, `<folder-list>` means one folder's own
  `TASKS.md`.
- **There is no combined file.** Merlin does not build one. To show everything
  open, read each folder's list in turn, in the order the `folders:` rows give.
  The engine's `rollup-path` command names a file nothing writes, so never open
  it or offer it.
- **The single list at `<task-list>` is frozen.** It keeps the tasks from before
  the switch. It can be read, and the engine refuses every write to it.
- **Pass `--registry <merlin-manifest>` on every engine command that takes
  it** (all of them except `list`). The engine sits in the plugin folder and
  does not find the business folder's settings file by itself.

## Adding a task

```
python3 <engine>/triage.py add --registry <merlin-manifest> \
  --tag <Folder> --text "**Short title.** longer description" \
  --section active --commit
```

1. **Leave out `--list`.** `--list` writes the named file and skips the router.
   Without it, `--tag` picks the folder: the row whose `name` or `legacy_tags`
   matches the tag.
2. **Use a tag a row names.** If the project has no row, ask the user which
   folder the task belongs in. A tag no row matches still lands: it goes to the
   folder named by `orphan_default`, with the tag kept, and the report shows
   `"orphan_routed": true`. Tell the user which folder it went to. `lint` will
   flag that tag as an unknown project until a row names it. `--tag General`
   is such a tag unless a row is named General.
3. **Read the report rather than assuming.** `id` is the new id, `list` the file
   written, `folder` the folder. The first task for a folder creates its list.
4. Leave off `--commit` for a preview. A preview reserves no id, so the id may
   differ on commit.

## Finding a task

```
python3 <engine>/triage.py find <id> --registry <merlin-manifest>
```

It prints JSON: `found`, `list` (the file that holds it), `section`, `closed`,
`writable`, and `hash`, the fingerprint of the line as it stands. It exits 1
when the id is in no list. Use it whenever you have an id and are not sure
which folder holds it.

## Changing a task

```
python3 <engine>/triage.py apply --file <folder-list> \
  --registry <merlin-manifest> --ops <temp>/ops.json
```

Preview first, then run it again with `--commit`, as above.

- **The engine re-routes by id.** Name any folder's list in `--file`. The engine
  looks up each id, writes the list that holds it, and says so in the report
  with `rerouted_from` and `rerouted_to`.
- **One list per call.** Ops that name tasks in two lists are refused with
  `multi-list-ops` and nothing is written. Split them into one call per list.
- **Two more refusals.** `unresolved-id`: the id is in no list (check it with
  `find`). `frozen-only-id`: the id is only in the frozen list at `<task-list>`,
  which can be read and not changed.
- **`expect` guards a line that may have moved.** Add `"expect": "<hash>"` to
  an op, with the `hash` from `find`. The engine compares it while it holds the
  lock. If the line changed since, that op is skipped and reported as
  `stale-expectation`. Run `find` again, show the user the new line, and redo
  the change.

```json
[{"tid": "WS12", "action": "close", "expect": "<hash from find>"}]
```

## Old prefixes

A folder that changed its prefix lists the old one under `legacy_prefixes` in
its row. Ids with the old prefix still route to that folder and are never
renumbered. New tasks there get the current prefix.

## Task numbers on this computer

In this mode each computer gives out only ids that end in its own lane digit,
so two computers can never give out the same id. Ids therefore skip numbers
(`WS3`, `WS13`, `WS23`). That is expected.

If `add` is refused with `no-lane` or `lane-machine-mismatch`, this computer
has no lane of its own yet. Nothing was written. Tell the user, in plain words,
and offer the one fix: the task numbers step of `merlin:setup` (the user can
say "set up task numbers"). It shows what it will write and asks first. Do not
run the command printed in the engine's message as it stands: it leaves out
`--registry` and fails here. The step runs, after the user's yes:

```
python3 <engine>/claim_id.py --enroll --registry <merlin-manifest>
```

It writes the lane file `~/.claude/merlin-task-lane`, outside the business
folder, and one entry under `lanes:` in `<merlin-manifest>`. Then retry the
`add`.

## Checks and repair

- **Lint one list:**
  `python3 <engine>/triage.py lint --file <folder-list> --registry <merlin-manifest>`.
  It reports open lines missing an id, a date or a project tag, duplicate ids,
  and titles over 100 characters. Exit 1 means violations. `--section` checks
  one section only and skips the duplicate-id scan, so never cite a `--section`
  run as proof there are no duplicates. A note that unclaimed ids were not
  checked is expected.
- **Repair missing ids or a missing counter:**
  `python3 <engine>/triage.py assign-ids --file <folder-list> --registry <merlin-manifest>`,
  then the same with `--commit` after the user's yes. It gives an id to each
  open line that has none and resets the counter. It is safe to run again.
- **Stale tasks:** run `stale-triage.md` once per folder list.

## A folder this session cannot reach

If the engine refuses with `no-folder` or `unreachable-folder`, the folder in
that row is not in reach from here (for example it has not synced yet). Nothing
was written. Do not file the task into another list instead. Write a pending
record in the open project's `updates/pending-ledger/` folder, one file per
change, named `<YYYY-MM-DD>_<short-title-in-kebab-case>.md`:

```markdown
---
status: PENDING
op: add
target: <folder name from its row>
store: tasks
recorded: <YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM>
---
--tag <Folder> --section active --text "**Short title.** longer description"
```

For a change to an existing task, use `op: apply` and put the `ops.json` array
under the frontmatter instead. Never claim or guess an id for a pending add.

Nothing delivers these records by itself. Tell the user the record exists and
where. When the folder is in reach again, run the `add` or `apply` the record
holds, then change `status:` to `REPLAYED`, add `replayed:` with the date and
the id the engine gave, and rename the file to end in `.replayed.md`.

## Switching it on

This is the user's decision. Never switch it on unasked. When the user asks:

1. Say what changes. The single list becomes read-only. Open tasks in it can no
   longer be closed or changed. So close or finish them first, or, after the
   switch, add each one that is still open to its folder with `add` and note
   its old id in the text.
2. The `task_lists:` block needs `state: active`, an `orphan_default` naming
   one of the rows, a `lanes: []` line, and one `folders:` row per project:

   ```yaml
   task_lists:
     state: active
     frozen_ledger: <as it was>
     orphan_default: Website
     lanes: []
     folders:
       - name: Website
         prefix: WS
         path: <the project folder, relative to this settings file>
   ```

   A prefix is two or three capital letters, never `T`, and no two rows share
   one. Show the user the edit and ask before writing it.
3. Each computer that adds tasks then needs its lane: the task numbers step of
   `merlin:setup`.
